tier_reason: C stands (rule for numbers measured on code later fixed for correctness bugs): the published VectorCos rows predate the 2026-07-19 replacement of kernels with up to about 6e8 ULP error.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the v1.5.x VectorCos rows (4.9x, 3.0x, 8.5x) were measured on cos kernels later replaced for accuracy bugs (NEON v1.4.0 Taylor kernel about 6e8 ULP with sign errors near k*pi/2, x86 about 3e5 ULP, issue #95); the verification tests cover only [-4pi, 4pi] at 1e-9 absolute tolerance. Only the NEON exp 2.5-2.6x row is current.

tier_reason: B stands; security flaws in the bundled ed25519 code documented.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the bundled orlp/ed25519 trusts a caller-supplied public key when signing (double-public-key key leak), checks only the top 3 bits of S when verifying (malleable signatures pass), uses SHA-512-expanded 64-byte secret keys incompatible with libsodium and tweetnacl, and frees key bytes from the wasm heap without zeroing; the bench never checks the verify result.

tier_reason: C stands; the only number is code size and the same paper reports the Souper-built Clang about 2% slower.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the paper's only output metric is code size (4.4% smaller Clang binary) and it reports the Souper-built Clang about 2% slower; the SPEC 2.32x is Souper's own analysis speed; open wrong-code bugs #311, #562 and #166 remain at archive.

tier_reason: D stands; signed-char bug in the scalar tails and a blind correctness check documented.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the scalar tails and the scalar baseline delete non-ASCII bytes on Apple arm64 (signed char compared with 32) while the vector bodies keep them; the generated test text is pure ASCII, so the check never sees the difference.

tier_reason: B stands on the TPAMI 2021 table; the committed scripts cannot reproduce the headline {8,8} rows or the baseline R@100 values.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the committed benchmark scripts run neither the {8,8} AVX-512 variants nor the 64-bit {4,4} AVX-512 variant, so the headline rows and baseline R@100 values come from runs not in the repo; one timed 10k-query batch; dequantised distances without re-rank; AVX-512 classes fall back to scalar silently.

tier_reason: B stands; the library default enables an adaptive heuristic, while the benchmark ran exact mode.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the library defaults enable the wf-adaptive heuristic (results not guaranteed optimal); the BiWFA benchmark ran wf_heuristic_none, so its numbers are exact; open #102 (suboptimal ends-free results) and #97 (OOM or segfault after millions of alignments).

tier_reason: Downgraded from A to C (asymmetric-harness precedent): ssw_test charges re-reading and parsing the whole Swiss-Prot FASTA per query and a suboptimal-score computation to SSW only, and like for like (parasail 'sat', same 8-then-16-bit strategy) parasail SSE4.1 is slower than SSW at 390 and 513 residues.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: SSW's timer includes FASTA parsing per query and the suboptimal score; like for like parasail SSE4.1 sat is slower than SSW at 390 and 513 residues (44.4 vs 41.5 s, 55.2 vs 48.7 s); open wrong-score issue #111; no AVX-512; stale since v2.6.2.

tier_reason: B stands; the replace-all win rests on row recycling, but the React comparison holds without the affected rows (0.635x).

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the keyed app recycles cleared rows and their <tr> nodes for new ids, so create-1k, create-10k and replace-all reuse earlier rows (the suite's keyed check misses it); without rows 01, 02 and 07 mogwai is still 0.635x React.

tier_reason: C stands; CTR-mode counter bug and non-standard counter layout documented.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: AES_128_encrypt_ctr does not advance the counter past the last block (keystream reuse across calls; fix in open PR #6); little-endian first-word counter does not match SP 800-38A (#1); the harness is one timed call with no known-answer check.

tier_reason: D stands; the artifact's micro-benchmark script disables SUD before timing the full configuration.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: bench_micro.sh's xstate run leaves SUD disabled and plot_micro.py subtracts the SUD overhead, so the full-configuration bar is understated; the headline row uses non-default SAVE_VECTOR_REGS 0; the artifact pins a commit before the 2025 redzone and xsave fixes.

tier_reason: C stands; anti-DCE check that cannot see the scan output, a mis-instantiated uint16 row and an unbenchmarked signed-LUT bug documented.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: the anti-DCE check reads an untouched buffer (Bolt writes a by-value copy); the 'uint16 safe' row instantiates NBytes=1 through a comma expression; the SignedLUTs uint16 path is wrong on half the rows; with fixed-size codes the speedup grows with N and accuracy is not measured; one thread on a 2013 i7-4960HQ.

tier_reason: A stands; virtualised-EC2 variance and the shipped config's disabled native backends documented.

corrections.caveats: Enricher: no-opt disables native arithmetic and native Keccak x4 together; native backends are off in the shipped config and chosen at compile time; up to 18% variance on virtualised EC2 (#429); open #1772 (no vzeroupper) and #1338 (stack use).
